problems.title: Powers with a common exponent
problems.question: Evaluate (a) $(2\tfrac23)^8(3/8)^8$; (b) $3^{16}2^{10}/54^5$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: (a) The product inside the eighth power is (8/3)(3/8)=1, giving 1.

problems.title: Multiply and collect polynomial terms
problems.question: Expand (a) $(x+y)(2x-y)(3x+y)$; (b) $(x^2-3x+1)^2$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Distribute every term and combine equal powers.
steps: (a) First two factors give 2x²+xy−y². Multiplying by 3x+y gives $6x^3+5x^2y-2xy^2-y^3$.
(b) Squares contribute x⁴+9x²+1; cross terms contribute −6x³+2x²−6x. Sum to $x^4-6x^3+11x^2-6x+1$.

problems.title: Area gained by increasing one rectangle side
problems.question: A rectangle’s length is twice its width. Increasing the width by 4 m increases area by 32 m². Find its original dimensions.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Area increase = unchanged length × added width.
steps: The length is 32/4=8 m. The original width is half of it, 4 m.

problems.title: Exterior angles determine all interior angles
problems.question: One of a triangle’s exterior angles is half another and 20° less than the third. Find the triangle angles.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: One exterior angle at each vertex totals 360°; interior and exterior angles supplement each other.
steps: Write the exterior angles t,2t,t+20°. Their sum gives 4t+20=360, so t=85°.
The exterior angles are 85°,170°,105°, hence the interior angles are 95°,10°,75°.

problems.title: Last digit of a power product
problems.question: Find the last digit of $3^{n+1}17^n$ for positive integer n.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: 51 ends in 1, so every positive power of 51 ends in 1. Multiplication by 3 gives last digit 3.

problems.title: An altitude divides a right triangle
problems.question: C is right, CD is the altitude to AB, ACD=2BCD and BD=3.7. Find AD.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: The two angles at C total 90°; projected-leg relation $AD/BD=AC^2/BC^2$.
steps: The split angles are 60° and 30°. Thus A=30°,B=60° and AC=√3 BC.
The projection ratio is 3:1, giving AD=3×3.7=11.1.

problems.title: An angle sum in two intersecting triangles
problems.question: In the source figure, AMN has angles at M,N equal theta,delta; PKQ has angles at P,K equal alpha,beta; BAQ=ACB=alpha. Find alpha+beta+delta+theta.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Triangle angle sum and supplementary angles at an intersection.
steps: Put BAC=t. Since BAQ=ACB=alpha, triangle AQC has angle AQC=180−t.
QP lies along QC’s opposite direction and QK along QA’s opposite direction, so angle PQK=180−t. In PKQ this gives alpha+beta=t.
In AMN the angle at A is t, hence theta+delta=180−t. Add the two results.

problems.title: An altitude is between the two hypotenuse pieces
problems.question: In right triangle ABC with altitude CD to hypotenuse AB, prove that one of AD,BD is at most CD and the other at least CD.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: Let u=min(AD,BD), v=max(AD,BD). Since 0<u≤v, multiplying gives u²≤uv≤v².
Taking nonnegative square roots yields $u\le\sqrt{uv}=CD\le v$. Equality throughout occurs when AD=BD.

problems.title: The minimum of a completed square
problems.question: Find the minimum of $(a+2b)(a+2b-6)-9$ for real a,b.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: The square is nonnegative. It vanishes whenever a+2b=3, so the lower bound −18 is attained.
